events.headline: Rico Dowdle sits out Monday and Tuesday practice with his toe; unlikely for Thursday night at Cleveland
events.detail: Dowdle (right toe) did not take part in Monday's walkthrough or Tuesday's practice, per RotoWire citing PennLive, after being inactive for the Week 3 win over Cincinnati. Pittsburgh plays at Cleveland on Thursday night, so there are only two more reports before kickoff. In Week 3 without him Jaylen Warren played 90% of the snaps and ran 17 times for 127 yards with three catches for 31 yards. Warren played through a shoulder issue last week and was not listed on the Week 4 estimated report.
events.so_what: Set Thursday lineups on the assumption Dowdle sits: Warren is a volume starter at RB or FLEX again, with a near-every-down share. Dowdle is a bench hold, and because the game is Thursday his status must be checked Wednesday night rather than on Sunday morning.

events.headline: Giants acquire J.J. McCarthy from the Vikings for a 2027 fifth; Jameis Winston stays the starter
events.detail: The Vikings announced Monday that they traded McCarthy to New York for a 2027 fifth-round pick, pending a physical. The Giants lost Jaxson Dart for the season to knee surgery (MCL, PCL and meniscus) in Week 2. John Harbaugh said Monday that Winston remains the starter with McCarthy on the roster, so McCarthy begins as the backup.
events.so_what: No immediate lineup change: Winston keeps the job, and with it the higher-volume, higher-interception passing that feeds Malik Nabers. McCarthy is a watch-list name only if Winston struggles; he is not a stash in a one-QB lineup.

events.headline: Baker Mayfield MRI shows no ligament damage, but Bowles says he misses at least three games; rookie Jalon Daniels starts vs. Packers
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 27 item. Monday's MRI on Mayfield's dislocated right (throwing) thumb found no fracture, tendon or ligament damage, per Ian Rapoport and Jeremy Fowler. Todd Bowles still said Mayfield will miss at least the next three games because the thumb limits his grip, and Mayfield is getting a second opinion before a formal timeline. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who finished Sunday's 23-16 loss to Minnesota, is in line for his first start at home against Green Bay.
events.so_what: Plan on no Mayfield through roughly Week 6, with the second opinion the only thing that could shorten it. A rookie UDFA starter lowers the ceiling of every Tampa Bay pass catcher and tilts the offense toward the run. Do not start Daniels in a one-QB lineup; anyone relying on Mayfield needs a streamer for the next three weeks.

events.headline: Breece Hall week-to-week with a quad injury after MRI; likely out vs. Bears, Braelon Allen leads the backfield
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 27 item. An MRI Monday showed Hall avoided a long-term injury to his right quadriceps, and ESPN and NFL Network sources call him week-to-week. He was hurt on the opening drive of the fourth quarter of the 31-24 loss in Detroit and is unlikely to be ready for Sunday against Chicago. Braelon Allen took over the backfield after he left.
events.so_what: Not a long absence, but plan on Hall missing Week 4. Allen inherits the early-down and goal-line work and is a FLEX start while Hall is out; he is the priority handcuff add in Tuesday waivers.

events.headline: De'Von Achane tears his left ACL, out for the season; Hafley says Dolphins backs will all 'have their roles'
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 27 item. Monday's MRI confirmed a torn left ACL, and ESPN reports Achane will miss the rest of 2026. He was hurt in the first quarter of the loss at Kansas City. Ollie Gordon, the only other active back Sunday, finished with 17 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown plus three catches for 14 yards, and receiver Malik Washington took some snaps at running back. Jeff Hafley said Monday that 'they're all going to have their roles,' called Jaylen Wright (stinger, foot) day-to-day, and said he and the GM will discuss adding a back this week.
events.so_what: Achane is a drop-or-IR decision now, not a hold. Gordon is the immediate early-down and goal-line back and the top Miami add, but Hafley's committee language plus a healthy Wright, or a signed veteran, caps him short of the every-down role Achane had. Bid on Gordon as a FLEX with RB2 upside, not as a like-for-like replacement.

events.headline: Justin Jefferson MRI shows an ankle sprain, nothing long-term; could play Week 4 vs. Dolphins
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 27 item. Monday's imaging on Jefferson's left ankle came back clean apart from a sprain, and ESPN's sources say he has a chance to play Sunday against Miami. He was hurt at the end of Minnesota's first possession in the 23-16 win over Tampa Bay, and Kevin O'Connell said afterward he was 'pretty close' to returning in that game.
events.so_what: Best-case outcome of the MRI, but a chance to play is not a clearance. Hold him and keep a WR or FLEX fallback ready until the Wednesday-to-Friday practice reports show whether he is practicing.

events.headline: Mike Evans day-to-day after Monday exam finds no significant rib injury
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 27 item. Evans was carted off in the second quarter against Arizona after a hit from Budda Baker; Kyle Shanahan said postgame they could not yet tell whether it was a broken rib or an oblique. Monday's full evaluation found no significant injury and he is considered day-to-day, though his Week 4 practice participation may be limited. He is also managing the hip that made him Questionable last week.
events.so_what: Better than feared, but a rib plus a hip is still a pain-tolerance question and the designation will not come until Friday. Keep a WR or FLEX fallback lined up and let the practice reports decide.

events.headline: Travis Etienne will miss time with his hamstring, Kellen Moore says; timetable TBD
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 27 item. Moore said Monday that Etienne will miss time after re-aggravating the left hamstring that limited him in practice Wednesday and Thursday. He left midway through the third quarter of the 35-27 loss to the Raiders after 13 carries for 57 yards. No timetable has been given, so injured reserve has not been ruled in or out.
events.so_what: Plan on at least Week 4 without him, and a recurring hamstring can stretch longer. Alvin Kamara is the likely early-down beneficiary; check which of Kamara, CJ Donaldson and Kendre Miller is on your wire before Tuesday bids.

events.headline: Jayden Daniels will practice this week and travel to London; Week 4 status still open
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 25 item. On Monday the Commanders said Daniels (dislocated left elbow, no surgery) will take part in practice this week and make the trip to London for the Week 4 game against the Colts. That is progress from last week, when NFL Network's Ian Rapoport called Week 4 unlikely, but nobody has said he will play. Marcus Mariota threw three touchdowns in the Week 3 upset of Seattle.
events.so_what: Practicing and traveling is a better sign than anything from last week, but it is still a forecast. Watch his practice participation Wednesday through Friday. Until he is confirmed active, a roster leaning on him needs a Week 4 quarterback, and the return is in a brace, so whether he keeps running (the konami part of his value) is the thing to watch in his first game back.

events.headline: DeMeco Ryans "hopeful" Nico Collins returns for Week 4 vs. Cowboys
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 25 item. Collins has missed two straight games with a Grade 1 hamstring strain. Ryans said Monday he is hopeful to get Collins and guard Ed Ingram back this week against Dallas. Collins would realistically need at least a limited practice between Wednesday and Friday to play. In Week 2 without him Dalton Schultz caught 12 of 14 targets for 140 yards.
events.so_what: Optimism, not a clearance. Hold Collins and check Wednesday's practice report; a limited session or better makes him a start against Dallas. If he returns, Schultz goes back to a secondary option and Xavier Hutchinson loses most of his volume.

events.headline: Puka Nacua missed Week 3; McVay "hopeful" he plays Week 4 at Philadelphia
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 25 item. Nacua (groin soreness, not a hip issue, McVay clarified) sat out the Sunday night loss at Denver, his second straight missed game. McVay said Monday the team remains hopeful he plays this week against the Eagles. TE Terrance Ferguson, who drew 29% of the targets in Week 2 without Nacua, is now likely out with an ankle sprain.
events.so_what: Nacua is still a hold, not a sell. Watch midweek practice: a return makes him a start, and with Ferguson likely out the targets concentrate further on Nacua and Davante Adams.

events.headline: Case Keenum throws two TDs and runs for a third as Bears rout Eagles 27-7 on Monday night
events.detail: Starting as the Bears' third quarterback with Caleb Williams out (hamstring), Keenum completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and two touchdowns, added a sneak touchdown, took no sacks and threw no interception. D'Andre Swift carried 20 times for 84 yards and Chicago held the ball for 36:53. For Philadelphia, Jalen Hurts went 16 of 25 for 153 yards with no touchdowns and an interception; Saquon Barkley ran 15 times for 82 yards, 73 of them in the first half.
events.so_what: Keenum kept the Chicago offense functional, which protects Swift's workload: 20 carries is a lead-back share while Williams is out. Keenum himself is a two-QB-league stopgap only, since Williams is due back in a few weeks. Hurts' line (no TD, one INT at -1) is his floor game; one poor night against a good defense is not a reason to bench him.

events.headline: Terrance Ferguson likely out Week 4 with a medial ankle sprain; Colby Parkinson uncertain with an AC sprain
events.detail: McVay said Monday Ferguson re-injured the ankle in the first quarter at Denver, returned for two snaps and left again after his only catch, and is likely to miss Sunday at Philadelphia. Fellow TE Colby Parkinson suffered an AC shoulder sprain in the same game; McVay said "we'll see" on his Week 4 availability.
events.so_what: Ferguson is a bench or drop for Week 4 at a position where the leagues start only one TE. With both Rams tight ends hurt, neither is a streaming answer this week; look elsewhere for a one-week TE.

events.headline: Commanders re-sign Austin Ekeler for depth; Rachaad White played through a shoulder injury
events.detail: Washington is signing Ekeler, pending a physical, back from the Achilles tear that ended his 2025 in Week 2. Team sources say the move was decided Saturday and is unrelated to Rachaad White's shoulder injury, which he suffered in the first half against Seattle before returning. The backfield is White (third downs, 151 scrimmage yards), Jacory Croskey-Merritt (team-high 142 rushing yards) and rookie Kaytron Allen.
events.so_what: Depth signing, not a role change: nobody in this backfield loses a lineup spot today. It does make the Washington committee even harder to start with confidence, and White's shoulder is the item to watch on the Wednesday report.

events.headline: Jalen Coker has a minor quad strain, considered questionable for Week 4 vs. Lions
events.detail: Coker left early in the third quarter of the 21-18 loss to Cleveland after two catches for 18 yards. Dave Canales said the quad "lit up on him" and the team would not send him back out after testing his strength. Reports call it a minor strain, and he was already playing through an ankle injury.
events.so_what: Questionable, not out. Hold him and read the practice reports; with two lower-body issues at once, a limited week makes him a risky flex rather than a locked start.

events.headline: Bucky Irving not injured and off the injury report, Bowles says, after sitting out the final drive
events.detail: Irving spent a long stretch of the fourth quarter on the sideline in the loss to Minnesota, prompting speculation about an injury. Todd Bowles said Monday he is not injured and is not on the injury report; Bowles did not explain why Irving sat late.
events.so_what: Start him as usual. With Baker Mayfield out at least three weeks and rookie Jalon Daniels at quarterback, expect Tampa Bay to lean on the run, which helps Irving's volume even if the offense scores less.

events.headline: Raiders WR Jack Bech breaks his forearm vs. Saints and is headed to injured reserve
events.detail: Bech fractured his forearm in the second quarter and was ruled out early in the third. Ian Rapoport reports he is headed to IR, which means at least four games missed; the injury is not expected to end his season. He had five catches for 48 yards and a touchdown through two games.
events.so_what: Bech was a depth receiver for fantasy, so the real question is where his snaps go in the Las Vegas WR room. Safe to drop unless you have an open IR slot.

events.headline: Mark Andrews returns for the second half vs. Cowboys after leaving with a hand injury
events.detail: Andrews left in the second quarter of the Ravens' game against Dallas in Rio de Janeiro with a hand injury and was listed questionable to return. He came back for the second half. He had one catch for 9 yards on three targets before leaving.
events.so_what: Returning in the same game is the best signal available; keep him in TE plans for Week 4 but read the midweek practice report, since hand injuries can limit catch volume even when a player suits up.

events.headline: Jalen McMillan ruled out vs. Vikings after re-injuring his left knee in the first quarter
events.detail: McMillan torqued the same left knee that cost him most of training camp and the season opener, left in the first quarter after one target and no catches, and was ruled out for the rest of the game. Tez Johnson and rookie third-rounder Ted Hurst are the candidates for his snaps.
events.so_what: A recurring knee on a player who only returned in Week 2 makes him a bench or drop until he practices fully. Tez Johnson is the speculative add if the injury costs McMillan more time, but neither replacement has a set role yet.

events.headline: Marcus Mariota throws three TDs as Commanders upset Seahawks 33-31
events.detail: Starting for the injured Jayden Daniels, Mariota completed 19 of 31 for 183 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, and Kain Medrano returned an interception 50 yards late in the fourth quarter to seal it. Daniels (elbow) is week-to-week and reportedly unlikely for Week 4.
events.so_what: Three passing touchdowns at 4 points each with zero interceptions is a usable streaming line on only 183 yards, so Mariota is a legitimate bye-week or injury streamer while Daniels is out, and he adds some rushing. It also keeps Washington's pass catchers startable rather than sinking with a backup.

events.headline: Jaylen Warren runs for 127 and adds 49 receiving yards as Steelers beat Bengals 30-27
events.detail: With Rico Dowdle (toe) inactive, Warren took 17 carries for 127 yards and caught passes for 49 more; a further long run was wiped out by a holding penalty. Michael Pittman Jr. played through the foot injury in his return.
events.so_what: Warren showed he can carry a full workload when Dowdle is out, 176 scrimmage yards against a backfield split when both are healthy. Start him while Dowdle sits; once Dowdle is back, this game is the argument that Warren leads the committee rather than splits it.

events.headline: Zay Flowers active vs. Cowboys in Rio after testing the hamstring pregame
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 26-27 items. Flowers (hamstring, Questionable) missed Week 2, returned to a limited practice Friday, and took the field early Sunday to test the hamstring. He is active for the late-window game against Dallas at Maracana Stadium, as is DT Nnamdi Madubuike.
events.so_what: He plays, so the question is volume rather than availability. A first game back from a hamstring can come with a snap count, so treat him as a WR2 with a lower floor this week rather than his usual role; Rashod Bateman loses the bump he would have had if Flowers sat.

events.headline: Michael Pittman active vs. Bengals; foot injury not on the Steelers' inactive list
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 25 item. Pittman was limited all week with a new foot injury and listed Questionable. The Steelers' official inactives (Joey Porter Jr., Rico Dowdle, Gabriel Rubio, Kevin Jobity, Drew Allar, Eli Heidenreich) do not include him.
events.so_what: Pittman is a start in his usual flex role. Limited practices all week mean some snap-count risk, so he is a floor play rather than a ceiling one.

source.label: CBS Sports live inactives tracker, Sept. 27

events.headline: D.J. Moore and Keon Coleman active vs. Chargers after game-time-decision tags
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 25 item. Both Bills receivers carried Questionable tags (Moore shoulder, Coleman ankle) and both are active on Sunday's list. Moore has not missed a game since 2020. Winds around 16-17 mph are forecast in Buffalo, short of a sit-worthy level.
events.so_what: Start Moore wherever he was your WR2/flex; no need for a pivot. Coleman stays a flex dart, not a lock, since the ankle may cap his snaps.

league_notes.clash: Moore and Coleman are both DrGMoney's.

events.headline: Tyjae Spears active vs. Giants; Tony Pollard already cleared
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 25 item. Spears (ankle) carried a Questionable tag and is active. Pollard was off the final report. The game at MetLife is forecast for heavy rain and gusts to 41 mph (see weather item).
events.so_what: Pollard remains the Titans back to start; the weather favors the run game. Spears is a change-of-pace flex only in the deepest league (Couples Clash).
